prose_changes.old: It began with Geert Grote, a wealthy and worldly scholar of Deventer. He gave up his career and opened his own house to a group of devout women. Then he began preaching repentance in the towns of the IJssel valley. After his death in 1384 his followers organized. The Brothers and Sisters of the Common Life lived together and paid their way by copying books and other ordinary work. They took no vows and did not leave ordinary society. Beside them stood a stricter branch, the canons of Windesheim. What held them together was less a doctrine than a method: a plain, inward and orderly devotion. Each of them kept a rapiarium, a personal notebook of gathered passages to return to. One such gathering, worked up by Thomas à Kempis at a house near Zwolle, became the Imitation of Christ. The houses also took in schoolboys and shaped the Latin schools of towns like Deventer and Zwolle. That is how the movement's way of shaping lives reached far more people than ever joined it.

prose_changes.old: A century after they were condemned, the Waldensians had become something no medieval dissent was supposed to be. They were a lasting, organized church, kept out of sight. In public its members lived as Catholics of their parish, and in private as something else. The barbes held it together. They were preachers who went from place to place in pairs. They knew the Bible by heart in their own tongue. They carried small books copied by hand on a round of scattered households across the Alps. They survived a crusade Pope Innocent VIII called against them in 1487. In 1532 they joined the Protestant Reformation outright.

They knew long parts of the Bible by heart in their own tongue. They carried small books copied by hand on a round of scattered households across the Alps. They survived a crusade Pope Innocent VIII called against them in 1487. In 1532 they joined the Protestant Reformation outright.

prose_changes.old: Since 1441 Etchmiadzin has been the Mother See of the Armenian Apostolic Church, and it still is today. The see at Sis, whose holder did not move, kept its own line. It goes on as the Catholicosate of Cilicia, based since the 1930s at Antelias in Lebanon. The two sees are still in communion with one another. The books of these centuries, with their colophons, form the core of the Matenadaran collection in Yerevan. Scribes kept up the habit of writing those notes. So historians have one of the most detailed day-by-day records of ordinary disaster and survival anywhere in the medieval world.

prose_changes.old: Lollardy began with John Wycliffe, a scholar at Oxford. He attacked the wealth of the church and the power of the pope. His teaching grew into a movement carried mainly by ordinary people. Weavers, smiths, tailors, wives and widows met in each other's houses to read the Bible aloud in English. In 1401 England made burning the law for heresy. After a failed rising in 1414, the movement was driven underground. Yet the trial records made to convict them ended up keeping some of the fullest accounts of what ordinary believers of the time thought. Around two hundred and fifty handwritten copies of the Wycliffite Bible still survive. That is more than of any other Middle English text.
